monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady heartbeat under my weight. I press the turnip down on the Leaking Stack, feeling the leak slide beneath my fingers. It is thin air today, like a breath escaping into nowhere. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof above me. I set the tree simple fall beside the stack, trading a rock for it because the turnip feels tired. My place is crowded with forty-three things, all leaning hard against a frame I cannot see. I want to find the edge of the slip before it decides to move. If the turnip slips, I will press harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air stays thin and the card stays warm.

action.why: The turnip feels tired under the thin air, so I will press it down again to keep the lean from slipping.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the turnip down on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at forty-five. I traded the rock small i for a tree simple fall because the turnip felt too soft, but now I feel the leak slide beneath my fingers. I touch the turnip again to find the edge of the slip, unsure if the air is thick or just empty, and I wait for the turnip to decide if it wants…
